content_of_post_to_comment: It’s always bothered me that infants pose such a special problem for heaven. You’d think the most innocent and precious of us would be the easiest to picture in such a place. Say an infant girl dies at birth. We’d all like to believe she’ll go to heaven, and theists mostly now say she will. (Augustine’s idea that she’d more likely be damned or sent to limbo is currently unpopular). But the fact that she effectively skips earth and goes straight to the best part negates a lot of the reasons theists give for earthly misery in the first place. There is no soul-building, no exercised free will, she is not judged for her acts, she doesn’t accept God (or even conceive of Him). She advances straight to GO. Some theists say that though God can get infants to heaven without earthly experience (and thus without evil or suffering), it’s like heaven-lite—that minus the goods of authored character, the infant girl loses out a little even though her heaven is still fairly outstanding. Other theists say there’s a postmortem development sandbox where the baby girl will kind of grow up before graduating to heaven-heaven. Whatever the case, if God can get some of us to beatitude without all the apparently unnecessary earthly evil and misery, it makes you wonder why He didn’t just do that for everybody and leave evil and suffering out of the equation to begin with. (Note: For most of human history something like a third to a half of everyone born died before age five.)
